source_text:
Appendices ad indices apostolorum discipulorumque
126 Τιμόθεος ὁ ἐπίσκοπος Ἐφέσου κατασταθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου ἐξ
ἐθνῶν ἦν, οὐκ ἐκ περιτομῆς, ᾧ καὶ πολλὰ μαρτυρεῖ Παῦλος νουθετῶν τὴν καλὴν
ὁμολογίαν τοῦ δοθέντος αὐτῷ χαρίσματος φυλάξαι, ὃς καὶ ἐνδόξως ἐκεῖ
ἐμαρτύρησεν. 127 Τίτος ἐπίσκοπος Κρήτης αὐτοῖς τοῖς Κρησὶ καὶ ταῖς πέριξ νήσοις
ἐκήρυξε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ κυρίου κἀκεῖ θανὼν ἐτάφη. Κρήσκης ἐν Γαλλίαις
ἐκήρυξε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ κυρίου κἀκεῖ θάπτεται. Ὁ εὐνοῦχος Κανδάκης τῆς
βασιλίσσης Αἰθιόπων ἐν Ἀραβίᾳ τῇ εὐδαίμονι καὶ ἐν Ταπροβάνῃ νήσῳ καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ
ἐρυθρᾷ ἐκήρυξε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, λόγος δὲ ἔχει καὶ
μεμαρτυρηκέναι αὐτὸν ἐνδόξως καὶ ταφῆναι ἐκεῖ· καί ἐστιν αὐτοῦ τὸ κοιμητήριον
ὅπλον ἀκαταμάχητον τοῖς πιστοῖς ἀλιτηρίων βαρβάρων, φυγαδευτήριον νόσους
ἀπελαῦνον καὶ ἰάματα ἐνεργοῦν ἕως καὶ σήμερον.
thought_title: Where early preachers preached, died, and were buried
orientation: The work opens by recording where several early Christian figures preached the gospel, died, and were buried, beginning with Timothy, bishop of Ephesus.
pass_a_gloss: Timothy, the bishop of Ephesus, appointed by the blessed Paul, was from the Gentiles, not from circumcision, to whom also Paul bears much witness, admonishing him to guard the good confession of the grace given to him, who also gloriously was martyred there. Titus, bishop of Crete, preached the gospel of the Lord to the Cretans themselves and to the surrounding islands, and having died there was buried. Crescens preached the gospel of the Lord in the Gauls, and there he is buried. The eunuch of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, preached the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ in Arabia Felix and on the island of Taprobane and in all the Red Sea region, and the account has it that he also was gloriously martyred and was buried there; and his tomb is an unconquerable weapon for the faithful against destructive barbarians, a refuge driving away diseases and working healings even until today.

choices.term: ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἦν, οὐκ ἐκ περιτομῆς
choices.english: was from the Gentiles, not from circumcision
choices.why: Keeps the literal contrast between the two prepositional phrases, preserving the ethnic and ritual distinction Paul makes.
rejected: was a Gentile, not a Jew
was of the nations, not of the circumcision

choices.why: Literal rendering of the phrase, echoing the Pauline language of 1 Timothy 6:12.
Uses the glossary sense for μαρτυρέω as dying for the faith, with the adverb rendered literally.
Renders the impersonal idiom literally, indicating a tradition or report rather than direct assertion.
Literal rendering of the military metaphor for the tomb's protective power.
Keeps the noun and participial construction literally, preserving the tomb's dual function as refuge and healer.
rejected: a place of refuge that expels diseases

pass_b_english: Timothy, the bishop of Ephesus, was appointed by the blessed Paul. He came from the Gentiles, not from the circumcision, and Paul bears much witness to him, urging him to keep the good confession of the grace that had been given to him. In Ephesus he was gloriously martyred.
Titus was bishop of Crete. He preached the gospel of the Lord to the Cretans themselves and to the surrounding islands, and he died and was buried there.
Crescens preached the gospel of the Lord in Gaul, and there he is buried.

The eunuch of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, preached the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ in Arabia Felix, on the island of Sri Lanka, and throughout the Red Sea region. The account has it that he too was gloriously martyred and buried there. His tomb remains an unconquerable weapon for the faithful against accursed barbarians, a refuge that drives away diseases and works healings even to this day.

problems.why: ἀλιτηρίων means 'accursed, impious, wicked' not specifically 'sinners'; 'accursed barbarians' or 'impious barbarians'

fixed: Changed 'barbarous sinners' to 'accursed barbarians' because ἀλιτηρίων means 'accursed, impious, wicked', not specifically 'sinners'.

last_rejected.quote: The account has it that he too was gloriously martyred
last_rejected.source_quote: λόγος δὲ ἔχει καὶ μεμαρτυρηκέναι αὐτὸν ἐνδόξως
last_rejected.why: Source says 'word/account has it that he was martyred' (uncertain tradition), English makes it direct fact by omitting 'λόγος δὲ ἔχει' (the account has it).
last_rejected.fix: The account has it that he too was gloriously martyred and buried there.
last_rejected.ruling: English includes 'The account has it that' translating 'λόγος δὲ ἔχει'; no omission; meaning preserved.
